I've been working this land for 40 years. My body isn't what it was — I'm 72 now, alone, and I need to be practical about what I can manage on 1.2 mu by myself. Luckily the wheat-maize rotation is what everyone around here does, so the same plot runs wheat through winter and maize through summer. I don't need to think too hard about the system — just execute it.

For wheat, I'll plant in mid-October like always, using an improved variety. Jimai-type seeds have been reliable here in Quzhou for years. I apply a full plough before seeding — I always plough for wheat, it's worth the work once. I'll put down base fertilizer at planting and topdress at jointing. I'll irrigate three times: the winter freeze watering in November to protect roots, jointing stage in April, and grain filling in May. Two pesticide passes — herbicide in the winter and one spray for aphids and rust in spring. I expect around 400 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

For maize, I turn around quick after wheat harvest in June. Rotary tillage only — no time or energy for a full plough in summer. I plant hybrid seed, the kind I've been using for the last decade or so — better yield than the old varieties. Maize doesn't need as much hand-holding once it's in. Two irrigations, one herbicide spray right after emergence. I'll put down more nitrogen on the maize — it's a heavy feeder. Expect around 550 kg per mu.

At my age, with just one person in the household, this is enough. I'm not trying to expand or experiment. I just want a clean crop and manageable workload.
